decisions.question: Where should the repo-defaults config file live in a target repo?

options.label: .egg/repositories.yaml (Recommended — matches existing repo-side .egg/ schemas dir and leaves room for future repo-scoped egg artifacts)
egg.yaml at the repo root (visible in `ls`, easy to mention in docs, but adds top-level clutter)
.egg.yaml at the repo root (compromise: hidden but single-file, discoverable via `ls -a`)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should we ship all four changes (schema simplification, layered config, onboard skill, validator) together as one feature, or sequence them as independent PRs?

options.label: Sequence as separate PRs in dependency order (Recommended) — schema+validator first, then layered loader, then skill. Smaller PRs, rollbackable.
One coordinated feature — all four together with shared tests/docs. Single migration story but larger blast radius.
Two phases: (a) schema-simplification + validator together, (b) layered config + skill together — two PRs instead of three or four
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should the unified `persist:` list classify entries?

options.label: By leading slash — entry starting with `/` is absolute (system dir), otherwise repo-relative (Recommended; matches the issue proposal). Simple rule, easy to teach.
Explicit per-entry tag (e.g. `- {path: /usr/local/bin, scope: system}`) — verbose but unambiguous
Keep two separate lists, just rename them `persist_repo:` and `persist_system:` — less migration risk, but doesn't simplify
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What should the deprecation policy be for the legacy schema (`persist_dirs`/`persist_system_dirs`/explicit `watch_files`)?

options.label: Accept both legacy and new schemas indefinitely — no migration pressure, dual code paths kept forever
Accept both, emit a one-line warning when legacy keys are used (Recommended) — nudge migration without breaking anyone
Accept both for two releases, then hard-deprecate — forces cleanup but creates a hard cutover
Hard-deprecate immediately and ship `egg config migrate` — cleanest schema but biggest disruption
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Where should the centralized merge loader live (the single import point that returns a merged repo+user view)?

options.label: New module `shared/egg_config/repos.py`, imported by `config/repo_config.py` and `sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py` (Recommended) — keeps the existing `config/repo_config.py` API but moves the read+merge into a shared package both runtimes already depend on.

Add the merge inside `config/repo_config.py::_load_config` and have sandbox import from `config/`. Simpler diff, but `sandbox/egg_lib` doesn't currently import from `config/`, which crosses the runtime boundary.
Brand-new top-level package `egg_repo_config/` separate from both — cleanest separation but adds a new package surface.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should the validator be exposed to users?

options.label: Both: a new `egg validate-config` CLI subcommand AND extend the existing `mcp__egg__validate_config` MCP tool (Recommended) — covers humans and agents in one change. Note: today's `validate_config` MCP tool validates *pipeline* configs, so this requires renaming or namespacing.
Add new CLI command only (`egg validate-config`) — simple, no MCP-tool name collision to resolve
Add new MCP tool only (`mcp__egg__validate_repo_config`) — fits the agent workflow but humans still have no CLI
Reuse `scripts/validate-config.py` and extend it to also validate `repositories.yaml` — minimal new surface area
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should the onboarding logic be delivered?

options.label: A new `/onboard-repo <path>` skill (under `skills/onboard-repo/SKILL.md`) (Recommended) — consistent with existing `/egg-setup`, `/sdlc`, etc. AskUserQuestion-driven so the human confirms detection.
A new `egg onboard <repo-path>` CLI subcommand — scriptable, headless. No interactive confirmation step.
Both — skill is the conversational on-ramp, CLI is the underlying detector. Skill calls CLI for the analysis pass.
Extend existing `/egg-setup --update repos` instead of new skill — fewer entry points but conflates whole-system setup with single-repo onboarding.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: When the onboard skill cannot write to the target repo (e.g. agent has no permission, or user runs it against a read-only checkout), what should it do?

options.label: Print the YAML to stdout and offer to append it to `~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml` instead (Recommended) — matches the issue proposal; user keeps onboarding even when checkin is blocked
Always write to `~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml` regardless — simpler but defeats the layered model
Always write to `<repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml` — fail loudly when permissions are missing, force the user to fix them
Write to a tmp path and print instructions for the user to copy it where they want — most flexible, least automated
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What policy should we adopt for list-merge semantics on layered fields (`checks`, `persist`, `watch_files`, `extra_packages.apt`/`dnf`, `local_repos.paths`)?

options.label: Replace by default; ship without an `extends:` keyword for now (Recommended) — matches the issue proposal's preference. Simplest to teach. Revisit if duplication shows up across the fleet.
Replace by default; ship `extends: true` (or `+` prefix) opt-in for additive merging from day one — future-proofs but adds surface to the schema before we know if it's needed
Append-merge by default — most ergonomic for additive cases (e.g. user wants to add an extra check on top of repo defaults) but the most surprising and the issue explicitly cautions against it
Pick per-field defaults: `extra_packages.*` and `local_repos.paths` append; `checks`, `persist`, `watch_files` replace — most ergonomic but most rules to memorize
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: When the user file lacks the per-repo block but the repo file is present (and operator-scoped fields like `writable_repos` still need to be set), should the loader implicitly trust repo-defaults or require the operator to opt in?

options.label: Loader auto-discovers `<repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml` when the operator runs egg against a checkout (Recommended) — matches the issue proposal's silent-skip-if-absent design. No opt-in friction for the common case.
Operator must explicitly list the repo in `repo_settings:` (or set a `use_repo_defaults: true` flag) before the repo file is read — explicit but defeats the zero-config win
Loader reads repo file by default but only for repos in `local_repos.paths` (i.e. those the operator has already vouched for) — middle ground
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the validator be strict (errors fail the load) or advisory (warnings logged, load succeeds)?

options.label: Two tiers — errors block (e.g. malformed YAML, missing required key, persist of denied path) and warnings advise (e.g. `make` target not found in Makefile heuristic) (Recommended). Matches existing validator patterns in `shared/egg_config/`.
All errors — hard-fail the load on any flagged issue. Safest but breaks users on heuristic false positives.
All warnings — log everything, never block. Lenient but undermines the 'catch at write-time' goal.
Strict at config-write time (`egg validate-config`), advisory at load time. Best of both — user gets blocked when explicitly validating, agents/runtime see warnings.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should we ship a one-shot migration helper alongside this work?

options.label: Yes — ship `egg config migrate` that rewrites legacy `persist_dirs`+`persist_system_dirs` into the unified `persist:` list and offers to extract per-repo blocks into `<repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml` (Recommended) — lowers the upgrade cost
No — deprecation warnings only; users hand-migrate. Issue lists migrate tool as out-of-scope; honoring that scope keeps PR boundaries tight
Yes but ship as a follow-up after the core changes land
Just provide a doc page with sed-able snippets users can run — zero new code, but more friction
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should we adopt schema versioning (`version: 1`) on the new files from day one?

options.label: Yes on both files (user file + repo file) (Recommended) — cheap insurance now; loader gracefully degrades for newer schema versions. Issue's open-question list leans this way.
Yes only on the new repo-file (`<repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml`); leave user file unversioned. The repo file is the one committed to source control and most exposed to schema churn.
No — don't add a version key now; revisit if/when we make a breaking change. Avoids paying the cost preemptively.
Adopt a different versioning scheme (e.g. `apiVersion: egg.config/v1` Kubernetes-style, or semver string) — more verbose but more conventional
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the onboarding skill detect Rust/Java/Ruby projects, or stick to the languages already used in egg-instrumented repos?

options.label: Ship detection for Python (uv/pip), Node (npm/pnpm/yarn), and Go only (Recommended) — these match the example file's documented patterns and the egg fleet today. Add Rust/Java/Ruby in a follow-up when there's a real consumer.
Ship the full set listed in the issue (Python, Node, Go, Rust, Java, Ruby, mixed) up front — future-proofs but more code to maintain without confirmed users
Ship only what the egg repo itself uses (Python uv) and document how to extend the detector — minimal but the most fragile if even a webapp gets onboarded
Other (explain in reply)

questions.question: What's the upgrade-friction tolerance for existing operators? Concretely: if the schema changes, are you OK with a one-time `egg config migrate` step, or should the loader silently accept the legacy schema indefinitely with no nudge?

Are there any existing repos already onboarded that would need their per-repo block extracted into `<repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml` as part of the rollout? If yes, please list them so the migration helper (if approved in decision-12) covers them and acceptance tests exercise the layered path on real config.

What's the priority ranking among the four pieces if we have to drop or defer one? In particular, is the validator considered nice-to-have given that #2090 already hardens the build-time fail-loud path, or is write-time validation the highest-value piece?

The issue's 'Out of scope' list includes a repo template library (`extends:` from a built-in catalog of `python-uv`, `node-pnpm`, etc.). The proposal lands repo-defaults committed to each repo, which makes templates more attractive. Should the plan phase reserve a hook (e.g. `template:` field, or a stable schema for shared blocks) so a follow-up can land templates without another schema migration?

Are there validation checks beyond the ones listed in the issue (build_commands without matching persist, persist without producible source, missing Makefile target, manifest/build-cmd mismatch, missing local_repos paths, dangling writable_repos, unreachable checkpoint_repo, repo-file with operator-scoped keys) that you want surfaced? Examples worth considering: `auth_mode: user` without `GITHUB_USER_TOKEN` configured; persist of an empty directory; commands that exec curl/wget in private mode where network is locked down.

Should the onboard skill's heuristic detection always require human confirmation (e.g. AskUserQuestion to confirm each detected build_command), or auto-write when confidence is high (single lockfile, single Makefile target match)?
